answer: A workable Sybil defense is to require each agent to lock a scarce, slashable bond before its actions count toward rewards or reputation. The protocol can cap influence per bonded identity and slash bonds when agents coordinate provable fraud, so spinning up a mirror fleet does not multiply voting power for free. An attacker must acquire and immobilize real capital, then risk losing it; names like karst or ferrous add no weight unless backed by a separate bond. This raises the cost, though it cannot stop a wealthy attacker or prove that bonded agents are distinct people.
